title: The two-primary Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula in Selmer corank at most one
sections_read: Entire 12-alternation-imaginary, 1–411: conjugate central extension and scalar Bockstein alternation including quadratic ramification; elementary-divisor parity; imaginary-S3 CM comparator and simultaneous Selmer seed; exact central finite/singular switches and common descent multiplier; compatible residual/characteristic-zero evaluations and nonzero traces; central mixed coefficient, integral quotient and ordinary rank-one center.

Entire 13-real, 1–1101: real quadratic ring-class level; elliptic Selmer seed; real-circle Hecke detector; integral rank-two Hecke packet with multiplicities; residual transversality, integral alternating presentation and Pfaffian cofactor lift; repeated-factor divisibility; coefficient-order descent; paired/Pfaffian division; horizontal logarithms and separate integral input-clearing; Heegner identity, denominator intersection and detector primitivity; exact rank-one product anchor.

Entire 14-cyclic, 1–692: cyclic-cubic Selmer seed with F4-linear evaluation prescriptions; Eisenstein comparator; addressed conductor variables and integral curve divisibility; primitive ray-unit determinant from integral regular-to-primitive quotient sequences and regulator/class-number comparison; exact unramified logarithm lattice; Eisenstein primitive and complete order-to-ray label bijection; quotient unit, rank-one center and exact trace-factor cancellation.

Entire 15-conclusion, 1–129: exhaustive residual anchor classification; nonnegativity plus zero sum forces both twist discrepancies to vanish, and the positive twist comparison transfers equality to the original curve; direct CM branch; usual low-rank consequences and exact two-primary quotient; signed squarefree density corollary with separate manuscript dependency.
claim_as_stated: The read anchor branches claim a coprime odd twist h and imaginary split discriminant k with analytic product order one and X(E^h)+X(E^{hk})=0. A Selmer seed is not itself used to infer analytic rank; quotient units and nontrivial Heegner specialization precede Gross–Zagier.

The conclusion claims that s_2(E)≤1 implies analytic rank=algebraic rank=s_2(E), finiteness of the whole Sha, positive rational leading-term quotient and equality of its dyadic valuation with v_2(#Sha), preserving total real period and full Mordell–Weil lattice conventions. The assertion is only an exact prime-two leading-term formula.

The density-one signed squarefree-twist corollary additionally invokes Theorem 1.2 of the separate Goldfeld/Selmer-distribution manuscript; that cited result is not independently verified by reading this section.
proof_architecture: Conjugate Bockstein alternation is proved with a central extension and compact local defect formulas before applying parity. Exact central switches preserve a class-functional valuation while residual rank-two switches terminate. The CM central mixed coefficient retains the common denominator multiplier H; only then does integral divisibility become a quotient unit, transferable through residual congruences.

The real branch separates characteristic-zero logarithm identification from integral cofactor divisibility. The Pfaffian lift is integral before specialization; weighted row/input/projection factorizations retain the full product of potentially noncoprime traces. A residually nonzero clearing series and horizontal integrality remove the remaining denominator, producing the actual integral fixed class needed by the independent real detector.

The cyclic branch computes a primitive comparator using integral coefficient exact sequences, full weighted ray-unit sums and exact local logarithm indices. The CM order/ray-label comparison counts all primitive coordinates with one global sign quotient, avoiding a growing-degree normalization. Equality of high-character valuations gives equal residual Weierstrass orders; integral curve divisibility and congruence then yield a unit.

Each branch proves a nontorsion conductor-one Heegner trace from a rank-one center before invoking Gross–Zagier. Extra inert trace factors are canceled against the literal Frobenius-square singular determinants at the all-zero center. The conclusion combines anchors with already-proved nonnegativity and positive twist transfer.

limits: This is a complete first reading of the four explicitly assigned source files, not independent theorem validation. No assertion here certifies the central-extension, Pfaffian transport, cochain/limit, local logarithm, regulator, CM label, or cited classical and collection-manuscript arguments.

This reader directly covered only sections 12–15: 4 files, 2333 lines, 174545 bytes. The parent base receipt covers README/root/references and 01–07; a different reader owns 08–11. Those receipts are not silently merged here, and this receipt alone does not establish whole-manuscript full-body status.

The theorem scope is usual two-power Selmer corank at most one and the exact prime-two leading-term formula, with total real periods, full torsion-containing indices and the stated height convention. The density claim has an external collection-manuscript dependency.

The BA/non-BA status of pi remains unresolved. BA would require a uniform positive lower bound for q^2|pi-p/q| for all integers p and q>0; non-BA would require a sequence of such quantities tending to zero. None of the read mechanisms supplies either.

Outstanding transfer obligations are nonvanishing of an exact integer determinant versus analytic smallness of that same determinant, row rank over Q(Z), a common basis/lattice with controlled denominators, and quantitative column-height plus quadratic-occupancy bounds. No source analogy fills these gaps.
